body:
FROM THE P5 SUPPRESSION LENS, 2026-08-19, on the T186 branch. H1 in both directions.

1. THE CLOSURE GROUNDS ARE NARROWED TO THE POOL. channelGroundFor asks
   containerScope({containers:[pool]}), so membersOf runs once and grounds === [pool]:
   withNegationClosureAcross then asks only the pool's reactor. Requesting the PARENT does not have
   this shape — the parent is shared, so gw itself contributes and grounds === [gw, pool].
   withNegationClosureAcross exists precisely because "a strike of an admitted delta can live in ANY
   of them".
   STATE -> WRONG OUTCOME: the receiving store holds a negation of a delta served from the pool, and
   the reader of the channel lens resolves the struck claim as LIVE. Reachable when the receiver both
   channels a peer AND federates with them directly: the retraction lands in the primary while the
   channel is frozen or has not polled. The store lies upward — H1's own direction.
   FIX SHAPE: keep the pool as the member source, hand [gw, pool] to the closure.

2. THE SCOPE IS APPLIED ON gatherImpl ONLY. Two sibling read paths were not changed:
   - resolvePinnedImpl (the §17 Name@vN door on REST, and the renderer byte door) evaluates over the
     primary ground.
   - watchEntityImpl (SUBSCRIPTIONS) resolves from matFor, which keys the materialization on the
     PROGRAM name — the exact sharing the ordering fix closed for queries.
   A lens may be declared public. So: declare a channel lens public, and `query` answers from the
   pool while `subscription` answers from the RECEIVER'S OWN primary ground through the peer's gather
   body, anonymously. If the peer's body selects a context the receiver also writes at — the normal
   case for a shared program name — that is the operator's private claims streamed to a stranger.
   Code asymmetry CONFIRMED; the disclosure is PLAUSIBLE because it needs that overlap.

3. A CHANNEL IS RESOLVED BY PREFIX ALONE, AND PREFIX UNIQUENESS IS PER-CONTAINER. openChannelImpl
   checks injectivity against standingPrefixes(gw, into), whose lead is `channel:<into>:`. Both
   prefix->channel lookups then use .find on prefix alone (reads.ts and channelNameOf). So two
   channels in different containers may both take `alice`, and then:
   (a) a read of alice:Note resolves over whichever pool insertion order surfaces first — one peer's
       claims answer a lens blessed from the other, which the code comment says must not happen;
   (b) a curse recorded on one is invisible to the other's poll, so the standing sync re-blesses law
       the operator retired.
   The living name is `<prefix>:<alias>` and carries no container, so both aim at the same name.
   FIX: refuse a prefix already assigned ANYWHERE in the store, or key by (into, prefix) at both
   lookup sites. A partial fix landed on the branch (the filename digest); the LOOKUP is still by
   prefix alone.

READ CLEAN, and worth recording so it is not re-audited: the read-closed subtraction cannot revive
anything (condemnedClosure is already closed under negation targets, and adds targets by id without
needing them locally), and the asOf filter matches groundAsOfImpl's rule and runs after the closure.

HALF-OVERTAKEN (stale sweep, 2026-08-25) — read this before building: Findings 1 and 3 died in the T186 landing (#434, e664c98): channelGroundFor now applies the receiver's own strikes (src/gateway/reads.ts:208-223) and standingPrefixes went store-wide (src/federation/channel.ts:549-567, 'a real defect this fixes'). Finding 2 lives in reduced form: resolvePinnedImpl and watchEntityImpl now REFUSE a channel lens (reads.ts:331, 401), but the code itself says 'T193 carries the real fix, which is a per-pool materialization rather than one keyed by the program name' (reads.ts:314-315) — serving those two doors from the pool is still open.
title: The channel-scoped read closes negations over the pool only, and three doors never scope at all
